sentences.text: This appeal has been filed by the claimant in M.V.C No.592/2018 against the judgement and award dated 10.03.2022 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Chikkamagaluru.
2. With a consent of the learned counsel for both the parties matter is taken up for final disposal.

3. Claimant met with an accident on 26.08.2018 near M.G. Road at Chikkamagaluru due to rash and negligent driving of car bearing registration No.KA-18-N-6434 and he sustained grievous injuries which resulted in permanent disability.
With these reasons he prayed to award a compensation of Rs.26,50,000/-.
4. Respondent/insurer denied the contention of the claimant and disputed its liability to pay the compensation.

5. Tribunal framed the necessary issues, recorded the evidence and after hearing both the parties awarded following amount as compensation.
 NC: 2025:KHC:39576 HC-KAR  Particulars Amount in Rs.
Towards loss of future earnings 2,52,000.00  Towards pain and suffering 50,000.00  Towards loss of amenities 30,000.00
Towards attendant, nourishment and 12,000.00 conveyance charges.
Towards medical expenses 40,000.00
Towards loss of income during laid up 50,000.00 period and rest period Towards future medical expenses 25,000.00
The Tribunal assessed the income of the claimant as Rs.10,000/- per month and awarded the compensation.
The main grievance of the learned counsel for appellant is that the amount of compensation on the other heads are not adequate in addition to that income taken by the tribunal is much lower side.

7. It is contended that as per the petition averments claimant was earning Rs.30,000/- per month by working as a painting contractor, even if the tribunal has taken into NC: 2025:KHC:39576 Sri Nanjappa vs C D Mallikarjuna Urs on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168491255/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: HC-KAR account the national income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority it would be Rs.12,500/- per month.
Therefore, the tribunal has not awarded a just amount as compensation.
8. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and submits that there are no reasons to interfere in the said findings.
9. The only dispute in this appeal is that the income of the claimant taken was not proper and hence there is no need to reconsider other facts of the case.
10. As rightly noted by the tribunal, claimant was unable to prove his income as Rs.30,000/- per month.
Therefore, the tribunal assessed notional income as Rs.10,000/- per month.

Undisputedly,
the accident had taken place during the year 2018, following the national income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the national income of the claimant is NC:
2025:KHC:39576 HC-KAR taken as Rs.12,500/- per month.
On that basis compensation requires recalculation.

11. On recalculation of compensation under the head loss of future earning capacity due to permanent disability as well as loss of income during laid up period, claimant is entitled to enhancement of Rs.63,000/- + Rs.12,500/-, total Rs.75,500/- in addition to whatever amount awarded by the tribunal.
Claimant is also entitled to interest on said amount from the date of petition till its realization.
Undisputedly, respondents are liable to pay the same.
12. Accordingly, following order is passed ORDER i.
Appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The impugned judgement and award dated 10.03.2022 in MVC No.592/2018 passed by NC:
2025:KHC:39576 HC-KAR iii.
Principal Senior Civil Jude and CJM, Chikkamagaluru is modified.

iv. Claimant is entitled to enhancement of 75,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
v. Amount of compensation enhanced is marginal, therefore, entire enhanced amount is ordered to be released in favour of the claimant on due identification.
